extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions with associated passages and distractors.
extraction.license: Creative Commons Attribution-Non-Commercial 3.0 Unported (CC BY-NC 3.0) License
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv:1707.06209.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Two-step crowdsourcing process: (1) Crowd workers select a passage from filtered textbook paragraphs and write a question and correct answer. (2) Another crowd worker validates the question and selects/writes three distractors aided by model suggestions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small percentage of the passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 science study textbooks from online learning resources (CK-12, OpenStax, etc.) covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Rule-based document filter applied to textbook paragraphs to select simple declarative statements. Sentences were filtered based on lexical, grammatical, pragmatical, and complexity rules (e.g., filtering out questions, modal verbs, pronouns, specific lengths).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Task 1: Workers chose one of three filtered paragraphs and wrote a question answerable by it (no yes/no, 6-30 words, answer up to 3 words). Task 2: Workers judged if the question was valid for a science exam, then selected up to two model-suggested distractors and wrote at least one distractor themselves to total three distractors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 92.8% of questions passed quality control. In a qualitative evaluation, humans identified the real exam question over the crowdsourced one only 55% of the time (not significantly better than random guessing).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with Master's status. 175 workers participated in total.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Random forest classifier (scikit-learn) for distractor ranking.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Risk of falling into specific lexical and structural patterns when generating questions repeatedly. Model-suggested distractors were accepted more often for short answers and rarely for long answers.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Neural models do not outperform simple IR baselines on the multiple choice version. Some distractor predictions are misaligned in specificity or ungrammatical for multiword expressions. Direct answer version is smaller due to unreleasable source texts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, Testing for science exam question answering and reading comprehension.
